metaDescription: Six inverters and inverter chargers for Class A, B and C motorhomes, compared on continuous watts, transfer switching, remote control and battery current.
expertTake: The Go Power 3000-12 inverter charger is the best overall for a coach that needs a transfer switch with 50 amp legs built in, and the BELTTT 3000W is the value pick for a plain inverter. The SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W is the compact charger option. Buyers who expect a motorhome to run a rooftop air conditioner for hours without the generator should plan a lithium bank before they plan an inverter.
introParagraphs: A motorhome has an advantage over a trailer: it carries its own engine, which can recharge house batteries while you drive. That changes the inverter question from how to survive a night off-grid into how to power the cabin sensibly between charging sessions.

The best inverter for a motorhome fits the coach's wiring, charges the batteries when the generator or shore power is available, and handles the big, brief loads of coffee makers and microwaves. This guide compares units on exactly those points.

products.name: Go Power 3000-12 Inverter Charger
products.description:
A 100 amp automatic transfer switch rated at 50 amps per leg is the feature that makes this Go Power the right shape for a motorhome. Most coaches have a 50 amp, two-leg electrical panel, and a switch that passes both legs when shore power is connected means the inverter simply slots into the existing wiring. When the pedestal goes away, the inverter takes over the selected circuits.

The unit combines the inverter and a battery charger in one housing, and the integrated handles are a small but real help during installation of a heavy box. At 3000W it is comfortable with a microwave, a coffee maker and the entertainment system, and it is a better match for a coach than a plug-in unit because it is built to be permanently wired. Compared with the 2000W SUNGOLDPOWER it adds a full 1000W, and compared with the 3000W BELTTT it trades a lower price for the charger and switch.

Ownership is mostly about wiring discipline. Have the AC input and output routed by someone who understands neutral bonding, because a motorhome with an onboard generator often has two sources that must not be bonded twice. Set the charger for the battery type, check the terminals every season and keep the fan area clear in the compartment.
products.bestFor: Coaches with a 50 amp panel that need an inverter, charger and two-leg transfer switch in one box.
pros: 100A transfer switch rated at 50A per leg suits coach panels
Inverter and charger combined in one hardwired unit
Built-in handles ease installation of a heavy box
Established RV brand with wide installer familiarity
cons: 12V input makes the battery current high at full load
Needs proper neutral and ground handling in the wiring
Higher cost than a plain inverter of the same rating

products.name: BELTTT 3000W Pure Sine Inverter with Wired Remote
products.description:
Priced for people who want pure sine power without paying for a charger, the BELTTT 3000W is the value pick for a coach. It delivers 3000W continuous and 6000W at startup, and the 23-foot wired remote means the unit can sit near the batteries while the switch lives in the living area. The LCD shows live input and output figures, which helps owners learn what the coffee maker and microwave really cost.

It has no transfer switch or charger, so the motorhome's existing converter keeps handling shore power and a separate switch must handle source changes. Next to the 2000W SUNGOLDPOWER it gives 1000W more but omits the charger, and next to the Wagan 3000W it adds the pure sine output and an LCD at the cost of the established brand name.

At full load the BELTTT draws roughly 280 amps at 12 volts, so it belongs on a large lithium bank with heavy cables. Mount it with ventilation, route the remote cable away from the DC cables to avoid noise and set a low-voltage alarm on your battery monitor so a long microwave session does not run the bank flat.
products.bestFor: Coach owners who already have a converter and want a plain, clean 3000W inverter.
pros: Pure sine output at a low outlay
23 ft wired remote lets the switch live in the cabin
LCD shows input and output in real time
6000W peak covers most startup spikes
cons: No built-in charger or transfer switch
Draws about 280 amps at full load on 12V
Less-established brand with limited installer support

products.name: SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W 12V Inverter Charger Pure Sine
products.description:
Low-frequency transformer designs are heavy but tough, and this SUNGOLDPOWER inverter charger is a low-frequency pure sine unit that combines an inverter, charger and AC transfer switch. The charger tops out at 70 amps and can be adjusted from zero to full via a switch, which is handy when the bank is small or the shore power circuit is weak. AC priority is the default, meaning the coach runs on shore power whenever it is available.

Its 2000W rating suits a Class B or a small Class C, and the low-frequency design copes with motor startups better than lighter high-frequency units, thanks to a transformer that can ride out surges. For a larger coach it is on the small side, and it gives up 1000W against the Go Power 3000-12 while charging at a similar rate. It also has a built-in GFCI outlet, a convenient addition for exterior or galley circuits.

Expect weight and a hum from the transformer. Plan a solid mounting shelf, short cable runs and a fuse sized for roughly 190 amps at full load. Adjust the charging current down for small banks to avoid overheating the batteries.
products.bestFor: Smaller motorhomes and vans wanting a tough, low-frequency inverter charger with adjustable charging.
pros: Low-frequency pure sine design handles motor startups well
Adjustable 70A charger fits different bank sizes
AC priority by default keeps shore power in charge
Includes a GFCI-protected outlet
cons: 2000W is small for a large Class A coach
Transformer hum may be audible in the cabin

products.name: EFFORTWAY 5000W Inverter 12V with Wireless Remote
products.description:
A wireless controller and an LCD put a 5000W inverter within reach of the driver's seat or the bedroom, which matters in a coach where batteries live in a basement bay. The EFFORTWAY delivers 5000W continuous and 10000W peak, the largest pure sine-class figure in this group short of the Wagan 10000W. It has four AC outlets for plug-in use.

The real constraint is the battery. At 5000W the current is roughly 470 amps from 12 volts, which almost no single battery or cable can sustain, so the practical ceiling is lower than the label suggests. It makes sense only where the house bank is large and wired with massive cable, or where the inverter is used for brief high-load bursts. Compared with the 3000W BELTTT it offers more headroom for a heater plus a microwave, and next to the Wagan EL3742 it adds a wireless remote.

Treat it as a specialist tool. Fit a class-T fuse, keep the cable run very short and let the engine or generator run during heavy loads so the alternator supports the bank. The fan will be loud under load, which is worth remembering for a bedroom bay.
products.bestFor: Large coaches with a heavy battery bank that need occasional bursts of very high power.
pros: 5000W continuous and 10000W peak give large headroom
Wireless controller and LCD simplify monitoring
Four AC outlets for direct plug-in loads
Pure sine-class output for motors and electronics
cons: Needs a huge 12V bank and very heavy cabling
Fan noise is high under load
Newer brand with a short track record

products.name: Wagan EL3742 3000W Inverter with Remote Control

specList.label: Protections
specList.value: Overload, over-voltage, overheat, short, reverse polarity

products.description:
Wagan has been in the inverter business long enough that its units are widely known, and the EL3742 offers 3000W continuous, 6000W peak, three-prong outlets and a high-output terminal block. The terminal block lets you feed a fixed circuit, and the remote control port accepts a switch panel. Protections cover overload, over-voltage, overheat, short circuit and reverse polarity.

The lineup's other 3000W unit, the BELTTT, adds pure sine output and an LCD, while the Wagan relies on an established name and simpler design. Check the listing for waveform details before assuming it matches grid power, because many classic inverters in this range use modified sine output. Against the huge Wagan EL3748, this 3000W unit is far easier on a battery bank.

Ownership is straightforward: mount it near the batteries on a vertical surface, fuse it for roughly 280 amps, and tighten the terminal block screws once a season. Keep the remote cable short and use the terminal block for any permanent hardwire, not the plug outlets.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a recognized brand and a terminal block for a fixed circuit.
pros: Recognized brand with long market history
High-output terminal block supports fixed wiring
Remote control port for a switch panel
Reverse polarity and other protections included
cons: Waveform quality depends on the model, so verify before buying
No charger or transfer switch built in
Lacks the LCD found on newer models

products.name: Wagan EL3748 10000W Modified Sine Inverter
products.description:
Ten thousand watts is more than the typical motorhome can ever use from a 12V battery, and the Wagan EL3748 is best understood as a specialist machine. It is modified sine wave, which suits heaters, lights and simple tools and does not suit rooftop compressors or sensitive electronics. It has four outlets, a high-output terminal block and a remote port.

At that size the current would be in the neighborhood of 900 amps at full load, which is why nobody runs it flat out from a house battery. It is better suited to a coach with an alternator-fed, very large bank or to a work-truck-style install with the engine running. Compared with the 3000W Wagan EL3742 it brings more than three times the capacity but needs infrastructure that most motorhomes lack.

Owners should be honest about use. Install with copper bus bars, short cable and a fuse designed for the current, and keep the engine running for heavy loads. Most coaches would be better served by a smaller pure sine inverter.
products.bestFor: Specialist installs running big heaters or tools with the engine running.
pros: 10000W continuous is the highest rating in the lineup
Four outlets and a high-output terminal block
Remote control port for switch panel use
Good for resistive loads such as heaters
cons: Modified sine can harm motors and electronics
Needs a very large bank and extremely heavy cabling

buyingCriteria.explanation: Most motorhomes have two 120V legs on a 50 amp panel, and a single inverter feeds only one. The Go Power 3000-12 includes a 100 amp transfer switch rated at 50 amps per leg, which passes both legs on shore power. Plain inverters like the BELTTT 3000W need a subpanel or separate transfer switch to integrate.

An inverter charger, like the SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W with a 70 amp charger, does the converter's job too. A plain inverter such as the BELTTT 3000W leaves the existing converter in place, which saves money but adds boxes. Choose by whether your converter is already good.

Microwave, coffee maker and television together usually run 2500 to 3000W, which matches the Go Power and BELTTT. Adding a second large appliance pushes toward the EFFORTWAY 5000W. Do not size to the peak rating.

Coach refrigerators, chargers and electronics prefer pure sine output. The Wagan EL3748 is modified sine and suited to resistive heaters. If you are unsure, choose pure sine and avoid motor problems later.

A 3000W inverter needs about 280 amps at 12 volts, and a 5000W unit like the EFFORTWAY needs about 470. Lithium banks with high discharge ratings can deliver this, while lead-acid banks sag. Decide the bank before the inverter.

Inverter bays are often in basement compartments, so a remote matters. The BELTTT includes a 23 ft wired remote, the EFFORTWAY a wireless controller and the Wagan units a remote port. A remote saves battery by making it easy to switch off.

specDecoder.meaning: A transformer-based inverter that is heavy but tolerant of motor surges. High-frequency designs are lighter and less tolerant.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W is low-frequency, an unusual feature in this price class.

specDecoder.watchFor: The Wagan EL3748 lists 10000W continuous, but your battery will limit real use.

specDecoder.meaning: The amps the integrated charger sends to the batteries, which sets recharge speed on shore power or generator.
specDecoder.watchFor: The SUNGOLDPOWER offers up to 70A and the Go Power is also a combined unit.

specDecoder.meaning: A safeguard against battery cables being attached backward, which can destroy the inverter.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coach integration
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked whether each unit fits a motorhome's 50 amp, two-leg wiring and shore power switching. The Go Power's 100 amp switch scored highest, while plain inverters like the BELTTT 3000W lost points for needing extra parts.

howWeEvaluated.title: Output capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: Continuous ratings from 2000W on the SUNGOLDPOWER to 10000W on the Wagan EL3748 were compared with typical coach appliance loads. Higher is not better when the battery cannot feed it.

howWeEvaluated.title: Waveform and load compatibility
howWeEvaluated.description: Coach refrigerators and electronics need clean power, so pure sine units were favored. The Wagan EL3748 is modified sine, so it was rated as a specialist tool.

howWeEvaluated.title: Control and visibility
howWeEvaluated.description: We rated remote switches and displays because inverters live in hidden bays. The BELTTT's 23 ft remote and the EFFORTWAY's wireless controller helped.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership realism
howWeEvaluated.description: Weight, fan noise, protections and brand support came from spec sheets and owner feedback patterns. Established brands such as Wagan and Go Power earned credit for parts and installer familiarity.

cards.label: Inverter charger
cards.text: The Go Power 3000-12 and SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W combine charging and switching, removing the converter and extra boxes. They cost more but install cleaner.

cards.label: Plain inverter
cards.text: The BELTTT 3000W, Wagan EL3742 and EFFORTWAY 5000W only invert. They are cheaper per watt but need separate transfer and charging hardware.

howToChoose.note: Pick an inverter charger for a new install and a plain inverter if the converter is already healthy.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: An inverter charger with a transfer switch that prioritizes AC input, so the unit hands over cleanly when the generator starts. Charger current decides how quickly the bank recovers.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W defaults to AC priority with a 70A adjustable charger, and the Go Power 3000-12 offers a robust two-leg switch.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want a clean, permanent install with a charger and a 50 amp-compatible switch. The Go Power 3000-12 is the benchmark.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Your converter works and you only need a clean 3000W for the kitchen. The BELTTT 3000W covers it.

maintenance.why: Road vibration loosens connections. A loose terminal at high current heats and fails.
Corrosion adds resistance. Replace discolored cable before it overheats.
Dust blocks cooling and triggers shutdowns. Compressed air restores airflow.
Switch between shore, generator and battery to confirm clean changeover. A stuck relay leaves circuits dead.
Wrong chemistry settings shorten battery life. Match the profile to the bank.

faq.q: What size inverter does a motorhome need?
faq.a: For a microwave, coffee maker and electronics, 3000W is the usual choice. Larger coaches that want heating appliances may consider 5000W with a very large battery bank.

faq.q: Can an inverter run both air conditioners?
faq.a: Seldom. Two compressors plus other loads exceed most banks, and a single inverter feeds one leg of a 50 amp panel. Plan on one air conditioner on batteries or use the generator.

faq.q: Should I choose an inverter charger?
faq.a: If you are replacing the converter or building a new system, yes. It saves wiring and gives smarter charging, as the Go Power 3000-12 and SUNGOLDPOWER 2000W show.

faq.q: Does the alternator charge the house batteries?
faq.a: Often through an isolator or a DC-to-DC charger. Check your coach wiring, because the alternator can support heavy inverter use while the engine runs.
For heaters and lights, yes. For refrigerators, chargers and electronics, pure sine is safer, so reserve modified sine for simple loads.
It matters for startup spikes only. Continuous watts decide what the inverter can run for minutes or hours.
